what_its_for: Carbinoxamine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives. It may also help with symptoms of hay fever and the common cold.
how_to_take: Take carbinoxamine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or a glass of milk. Swallow extended-release tablets or capsules whole — do not crush, break, or chew them. For liquid forms, use the measuring device that came with your medicine, not a kitchen spoon, to make sure you get the right amount.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, and the form of carbinoxamine you are taking. Adults and children over 12 usually take 4 to 8 mg every 4 to 6 hours. Children's doses are smaller and based on their weight and age — always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's exact instructions for children. The extended-release form is usually taken every 12 hours. Never take more than the recommended dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store carbinoxamine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking carbinoxamine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, or narcotic pain medicines, unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting carbinoxamine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty urinating or no urination, severe dizziness or confusion, seizures, vision changes, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or hives. Also contact your doctor if your allergy symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: Carbinoxamine usually starts working within 30 minutes to 1 hour after you take a dose. You should notice relief from sneezing, runny nose, and itching fairly quickly. It works best when taken regularly as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over) may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, confusion, and difficulty urinating — use with extra caution and only as directed by a doctor. This medicine is NOT recommended for children under 2 years old due to the risk of serious breathing problems. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as it may not be safe for the baby. People with glaucoma, enlarged prostate, asthma, heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid problems, or kidney or liver disease should tell their doctor before using carbinoxamine.
